teapot_rock.title: Teapot Rock, a distinctive sedimentary rock formation in Natrona County, Wyoming, that lent its name to a nearby oil field that became notorious as the focus of the Teapot Dome bruhaha, a bribery scandal involving misuse of funds related to the Teapot Dome oil fields in 1921-22 during the presidential administration of Warren G. Harding
notes: Title, date and keywords based on information provided by the photographer.

Curiously, the fields were named, not for the rock formation but for the large, rounded dome on which the "teapot" stands. Over time, the features that gave the formation its name have been eroded by windstorms; the "handle"  disappeared in 1930 and the "spout" in 1962
Credit line: Gates Frontiers Fund Wyoming Collection within the Carol M. Highsmith Archive, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
